role: Supporting decomposition of the already-opened 201 system-level memory effects; no new primary claim or family-vs-trait dominance test.
question: How much of the previously labeled family-by-trait-specific/residual heterogeneity is stable across S3 and prune-only phylogenetic treatments, rather than specific to backbone treatment?

repeated_measure_model.stacked_rows: two rows per family x trait system: S3 rho and prune-only rho

primary_quantities.variance_family: stable family-level component across both backbones
primary_quantities.variance_trait: stable trait-level component across both backbones
primary_quantities.variance_system: stable family x trait-specific component across both backbones
primary_quantities.variance_residual: backbone-specific / estimator-specific within-system remainder under the common-residual model
primary_quantities.prune_mean_shift: fixed prune-only coefficient relative to S3

interpretation_rule: A large conditional_system_stability means that the dominant family x trait heterogeneity observed previously is reproducible across the two predeclared phylogenetic treatments; it does not identify a biological mechanism.

heteroskedasticity_sensitivity.transform: Within each backbone separately, z-standardize rho to mean 0 and SD 1, then refit the identical random-effects structure without the backbone fixed effect.
heteroskedasticity_sensitivity.role: Mandatory sensitivity to different S3 versus prune-only marginal variances; not a replacement for the raw-rho model.

leave_one_out.trait: Refit raw-rho model after omitting each trait once.
leave_one_out.family: Refit raw-rho model after omitting each family once.
leave_one_out.output: Range of conditional_system_stability and share_system_total; descriptive only.

hard_nonclaims: Do not claim family effects dominate trait effects.
Do not treat prune-only as an independent biological replicate; it is a second predeclared phylogenetic treatment.
Do not equate variance_system with causal family x trait interaction.
Do not reinterpret the failed spatial-turnover programme.
